steps.title: Bang-bang
steps.say: Full power until you're there, then nothing. That's **bang-bang control**.

steps.title: Open Robot.java
steps.say: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Robot` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

steps.title: Find autonomousPeriodic
steps.say: Autonomous code has its own method. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `autonomousPeriodic` and press Enter to jump to it.

steps.title: autonomousPeriodic
steps.say: Write the if/else inside `autonomousPeriodic()`. It runs on its own in Auto mode, no sticks needed.

steps.title: Start the robot
steps.say: Your code only runs once it's built and started.

waitFor.hint: press Start and wait for Running.

steps.title: Enable in Auto
steps.say: Pick **Auto** and press **Enable**. Robot code runs only while it's enabled.

steps.title: Where did it stop?
steps.say: Watch the distance as it drives. In AdvantageScope, search for `Distance`, then drag **Robot/Distance** onto the **Left Axis**.

steps.title: Past 2.0
steps.say: It almost certainly stopped a little **past** 2.0 m: when the power cuts, the robot is still moving. Bang-bang can't slow down smoothly. The Control Theory lesson fixes that with PID.
